title: Sequenced acknowledgement protocol and session resumption for SIEM bridges
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Replace the current best-effort webhook model for external SIEM sinks with a sequenced-ack + session-resume protocol to provide ordered delivery, deterministic deduplication, and faster recovery after transient outages. This ticket scopes the protocol design, server-side state model, compatibility shim for existing customers (Splunk/Datadog/HEC), and the rollout plan with feature flags.

Background: Customers integrating Redwood audit streams into third-party SIEMs have diverging requirements: some need strict ordering and at-most-once semantics for upstream deduplication, others prefer low-latency at-least-once with idempotent processing. Current implementations rely on retries and DLQs in the forwarder which leads to out-of-order replays and opaque delivery gaps during restarts.

Design summary:
- Session layer: clients (SIEM adapters) open a named session (session_id) per tenant+sink. Server assigns a monotonic session epoch and maintains a persisted high-water offset for each session.
- Sequencing: every outbound audit entry has (session_id, seq_no, event_id). seq_no is monotonic within session; event_id is a stable UUID for dedupe.
- Ack model: receiver returns acks of the form ack(seq_no) and optional cumulative_ack(seq_no) for efficient confirmation. Server tracks per-session ack window and retains un-acked messages for configurable retention window (retention configurable per project/sink).
- Resumption: when a client reconnects it presents last_acked_seq_no; server resumes sending from next sequence. If the ack is older than retention, server signals a resync_required error and offers DLQ/export path.
- Delivery guarantees: default = at-least-once with strong server-side dedupe using event_id; opt-in exactly-once-ish mode via ordered sessions + write-through commit API with client-side idempotency tokens (this requires SIEM adapter changes).
- Backpressure & flow control: receivers may return 429 with Retry-After or send flow-control headers (x-inflight-window). Server limits in-flight per session and globally to protect runtime.
- Failure modes: network partitions, long-lived receiver slowness, server restarts. For each mode we enumerate mitigation: persisted checkpoints, resumable sessions, DLQ retention policy, observability hooks, and operator alerting.

Compatibility: Provide a compatibility shim that: (a) accepts plain webhooks and maps to an internal ephemeral session for existing customers, (b) offers a migration mode where adapters can advertise support for sequencing via header. Documentation and SDK updates required (Go/Node/python SDKs).

Acceptance criteria:
- Protocol RFC merged (confluence) and reviewed by Security and Infra.
- Server change implementing session state, persistent offsets, and ack API behind feature flag.
- Compatibility shim implemented and end-to-end test matrix covering Splunk HEC, Datadog, generic webhook, and a mock SIEM that verifies ordering and dedupe.
- Load test demonstrating <5% added tail-latency at 99th pct for production traffic and DLQ fallback behavior validated.
- Migration runbook and customer communication draft ready.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: aligned with SecEng and Infra. Decided to prefer session-based monotonic seq_no vs vector clocks due to implementation complexity and customer expectations.
2026-02-18 - Proto: posted initial protocol draft in Confluence (link below). Requested review from Platform SRE and Product. Open questions: retention window default and DLQ ergonomics.
2026-02-24 - Trade-off: choosing default at-least-once + server dedupe reduces customer SDK work; exactly-once mode will be advanced as opt-in for customers that can change adapters.

2026-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-bridge/pull/422 implementing in-memory session store and test harness for session resume. Initial unit tests green. Needs persistence layer and integration tests.
2026-03-08 - Security review: preliminary threat model completed. Outstanding: KMS key scoping for persisted offsets and access controls around session introspection APIs.

2026-03-12 - Infra feedback: spike demonstrated checkpoint commit latency is sensitive under high write fanout. Plan: use WAL-based append log per-tenant and async checkpoint flush at configurable fsync rate.
Next steps: implement persistent WAL, extend SDKs with session handshake, add e2e tests, schedule canary with low-risk customers, and finalize runbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for session open/close/ack semantics; integration tests against mocked SIEMs verifying ordering & dedupe; chaos tests for partitions and resume; perf test comparing tail latency with and without sequencing under representative token distribution.
